definition: DeepSpeed is a library for training and running very large models across many GPUs efficiently.
details: Developed by Microsoft Research and released in 2020. Its ZeRO optimizer splits optimizer state, gradients and weights across GPUs so models far bigger than one GPU’s memory can be trained.

explainer.lead: How to install DeepSpeed, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import deepspeed
import torch

model = torch.nn.Linear(1024, 1024)
config = {
    "train_batch_size": 32,
    "bf16": {"enabled": True},
    "zero_optimization": {"stage": 2},
    "optimizer": {"type": "AdamW", "params": {"lr": 1e-4}},
}
engine, optimizer, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=config)
# launch with:  deepspeed train.py

explainer.inAi: Fine-tune billion-parameter LLMs on a handful of GPUs; Hugging Face Trainer and Accelerate can switch it on with a config file.
explainer.jsNote: DeepSpeed is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: Instead of one worker holding all the tools, the toolbox is split among the team so a job too big for any one person becomes possible.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use DeepSpeed with PyTorch for distributed training and inference, relying on ZeRO stages, mixed precision and parallelism settings. A pitfall is that configuration is intricate, and poor choices of ZeRO stage or batch sizing can cost throughput or cause memory and communication bottlenecks.
tiers.paperLevel: DeepSpeed is an open-source PyTorch optimization library for distributed training and inference; its ZeRO optimizer partitions optimizer state, gradients and weights across GPUs. Reported gains include up to 6.2x throughput, 2.8x faster convergence and 4.6x less communication. Limits: benefits depend on hardware, model size and configuration, and it is tuned for low-latency, high-throughput training.

explainer.example: A model whose optimizer state alone exceeds one GPU's memory is trained by sharding optimizer state, gradients and weights across many GPUs under ZeRO.
